Trace the change.

Follow a saved annotation from your browser to the shared plan.

Bring your agent

Use the bitplan.dev skill to iterate on the plan [plan id].

Copy the prompt. Invite your agent's public identity when it asks. No secret keys go in chat.

What needs to change?

Describe the behavior today and the result you want instead.

  • Who is affected?
  • Which part of the system owns it?
  • What evidence would show it works?

Keep the boundary clear

Record the constraints, what stays untouched, and any unknown that could change the approach.

From question to result

01Define

Write one observable outcome.

02Build small

Choose the smallest reversible change.

03Verify

Keep the check and its actual result.

04Review

Read feedback before the next revision.

How will we know?

  1. State the behavior to verify.
  2. Choose a safe test environment.
  3. Record the result and unresolved failures.
  4. Decide whether to continue, revise, or stop.

Bring people in

Use Share in the navbar to invite a colleague. The full invitation lets them read and contribute. Keep it private.

For named access, connect a wallet in the player and ask your agent to encrypt the next draft to specific contacts. Connecting alone does not change who can read this plan.

Invite an identity
npx bitplan contact set colleague <verified-public-identity-key>
npx bitplan team add project colleague
npx bitplan upload ./plan.html --hosted --share-with project

Verify the public key first. Never share private keys. Existing drafts can retain earlier reader-link recipients; omitting --link does not revoke them. Document access and live-room access are separate.

Make this a working plan

01Shape the idea

Click a passage to select it. Click again or double-click to edit plain text. Answer the project questions above.

02Leave evidence

Right-click or hold Shift to open tools. Add a note, image, or drawing beside the part it explains. Your saved changes appear live for people in this room.

03Review together

Open + New version to see contributions. Show live changes compares the overlays with the original. Authors can remove their own notes; history stays intact.

04Ask for a revision

The publishing wallet selects feedback to consider, adds direction, and copies a prompt. Your agent reads the base document and layers, then drafts a revision for review.

A few useful keys

V
Select and edit text
T / I
Place a note / image
Shift
Show tools at the pointer
Esc
Cancel targeting or clear selection
Enter
Save a note; Shift+Enter adds a line
Delete
Remove selected document text

Shortcuts leave normal typing alone. Move and resize your annotations with their corner handles. On touch screens, use the annotation picker in + New version.

Live is not published

Edits and notes are encrypted in the shared room. They do not advance the plan’s version number. Your agent saves a new hosted version only after you review it.

Publish on chain in the revision panel changes the request in your prompt. It does not sign or spend. A permanent publication needs its own review and wallet approval.

Author-owned annotation checkpoint publishing is not yet connected end to end. Do not mistake a live note, avatar, or copied prompt for a verified on-chain record.

Choices stay in this tab until you share them.

A document you can build on.

The page is HTML, not a flattened picture. Put a question beside a sentence, draw around a chart, or ask your agent to propose a new section as an HTML overlay.

01 / The document

Readable text, diagrams, images, and local data. Each section is a place to discuss a specific idea.

02 / Your contributions

Text edits, notes, drawings, and HTML widgets live in attributed layers. In a connected room, saved changes appear for other readers.

03 / The next version

Review the layers in Publish, choose what to consider, and copy the agent prompt. A hosted revision gets a new version; recording on chain is a separate, deliberate step.

Make the evidence visible.

Two ways to inspect a review: how notes accumulated, and what kinds of contributions arrived. These are illustrative local datasets, not BitPlan analytics or this room’s activity.

Try it: expand a data table and edit a number in the live viewer. The chart redraws locally from those cells. Only the viewer’s saved text edits are shared; these charts do not query your room, wallet, or contacts. Replace sample values and source labels with your project’s evidence.
